transcript.text:
Here's the full sequence of API calls to create a source and trigger an account aggregation.

## Step 1: Get an Access Token

Use the Client Credentials grant flow with your PAT's client ID and secret.

```bash
curl -X POST \
  'https://[tenant].api.identitynow.com/oauth/token' \
  --form 'grant_type="client_credentials"' \
  --form 'client_id="{clientId}"' \
  --form 'client_secret="{clientSecret}"'
```

Save the `access_token` from the response — you'll use it as a Bearer token in all subsequent calls.

---

## Step 2: Create the Source

The docs specify four required fields: Source Name, Description, Source Owner, and Connection Type.

```bash
curl -X POST \
  'https://[tenant].api.identitynow.com/v3/sources' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer {access_token}' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "name": "My New Source",
    "description": "Example source for HR data",
    "owner": {
      "type": "IDENTITY",
      "id": "{ownerId}",
      "name": "Source Owner Name"
    },
    "connectorName": "Active Directory",
    "connectorType": "DIRECT"
  }'
```

Save the `id` from the response — this is your `sourceId`.

---

## Step 3: Trigger Account Aggregation

With the `sourceId` from step 2, kick off an account aggregation:

```bash
curl -X POST \
  'https://[tenant].api.identitynow.com/v3/sources/{sourceId}/load-accounts' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer {access_token}' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json'
```

This triggers ISC to connect to the source and pull in all accounts. You can optionally pass a body to control behavior (e.g., disabling optimization). The response will include a task ID you can poll to check aggregation status.

---

**Summary of the flow:**

| # | Purpose | Method | Path |
|---|---------|--------|------|
| 1 | Get access token | POST | `/oauth/token` |
| 2 | Create source | POST | `/v3/sources` |
| 3 | Trigger account aggregation | POST | `/v3/sources/{sourceId}/load-accounts` |
